I agree with some of the comments here that number 4 (title rule) might be a bit too broad. If your main concern is making sure titles reflect their content, you might consider folding that into rule 2 (no click bait) and writing a clean and easy definition of what constitutes click bait. /v/gaming uses "[the] title is unclear and 'low-effort' with the intention of getting people to visit just to see what the content is".

Our reasoning is that as long as the title accurately reflects the content, it's not click bait. If the title reflects the content and it's just a bad post, then the problem is with the content, not necessarily the title. We're not so much concerned with "bad" or rambling titles, because those usually just get downvoated, but a misleading title can be a problem if the community decides to crack down on click bait or misinformation.

Rule 3- No harassment

This seems unnecessary because it will never stop some people from harassing other users if that's their intention.

Someone with controversial opinions could also easily accrue several personal attacks from another user over a short time without it being a dedicated and focused effort to harass them.

I expect this rule will invite more trouble than it's worth with users trying to involve mods in their petty disputes in an attempt to get one another banned... which only invites the creation of puppet accounts.

Let's not forget that Voat is a public forum dedicated to free speech and nobody has ever died from hurt feelings.
